text: The 'computable' numbers may be described briefly as the real numbers whose expressions as a decimal are calculable by finite means. It is possible to invent a single machine which can be used to compute any computable sequence.

An automatic computing system is a device with which certain instructions can be given, and which will then carry out these instructions automatically. The device requires a central arithmetic part, a central control part, a memory that stores both instructions and numerical data, and input and output organs.

The IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic (IEEE 754) is a technical standard for floating-point computation which defines arithmetic formats, interchange formats, rounding rules, operations, and exception handling including binary32 and binary64.

UTF-8 encodes UCS characters as a varying number of octets, where the number of octets, and the value of each, depend on the integer value assigned to the character in ISO/IEC 10646. US-ASCII values do not appear otherwise in a UTF-8 encoded character stream.

CS2023 organizes computer science knowledge into core areas including Algorithms and Complexity, Architecture and Organization, Discrete Structures, Foundations of Programming Languages, Operating Systems, Parallel and Distributed Computing, Software Development Fundamentals, Software Engineering, and Security.

An introduction to mathematical modeling of computational problems, as well as common algorithms, algorithmic paradigms, and data structures used to solve these problems, emphasizing the relationship between algorithms and programming and basic performance measures and analysis techniques.

Ownership is Rust's most unique feature and has deep implications for the rest of the language. It enables Rust to make memory safety guarantees without needing a garbage collector: each value in Rust has an owner, there can only be one owner at a time, and when the owner goes out of scope, the value will be dropped.

At any given time, you can have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references, and references must always be valid. Unsafe Rust unlocks five actions: dereferencing raw pointers, calling unsafe functions, accessing mutable statics, implementing unsafe traits, and accessing union fields.

Safe Rust is a sound language: no matter what, Safe Rust cannot cause Undefined Behavior. Unsafe Rust is the exact same language with the same semantics, except that the programmer assumes responsibility for upholding the compiler's aliasing, alignment, initialization, and lifetime invariants.

Objects in C have storage duration (automatic, static, thread, or allocated), scope, linkage, and effective type. Dereferencing an invalid, null, or misaligned pointer, signed integer overflow, or violating strict aliasing rules results in undefined behavior.

Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII) binds the life cycle of a resource that must be acquired before use to the lifetime of an object. C++20 introduces Concepts for constraining templates, Ranges for composable algorithms, Coroutines, and Modules.

Objects are Python's abstraction for data. All data in a Python program is represented by objects or by relations between objects. Every object has an identity, a type, and a value. Special method names (__init__, __iter__, __enter__, __exit__, __get__) define the Python data model protocols.

An ECMAScript agent consists of execution contexts, an execution context stack, a running execution context, a set of job queues (macrotask and microtask queues), and a heap of objects linked through prototype chains and lexical environments.

One of TypeScript's core principles is that type checking focuses on the shape that values have, sometimes called duck typing or structural subtyping. TypeScript's type system is erased completely at compile time and introduces zero runtime overhead.

C# is a modern, object-oriented, and type-safe programming language running on the Common Language Runtime (CLR), unifying value types (structs, Span<T>) and reference types (classes, records), generics without type erasure, LINQ, and task-based asynchronous programming.

The Java Virtual Machine executes class files using class loaders, a bytecode verifier, an interpreter, a Just-In-Time compiler, and automatic garbage collection under the Java Memory Model (JMM) happens-before relation, complemented in Java 21 by lightweight Virtual Threads.

Go is a general-purpose systems language designed with structural interfaces, explicit error values, garbage collection, and CSP-inspired concurrency via lightweight goroutines multiplexed onto OS threads and typed communication channels.

Kotlin enforces null safety in its type system by distinguishing nullable and non-null references at compile time, and provides structured concurrency through suspend functions, CoroutineScope, Dispatchers, and cold asynchronous Flows.

Swift combines protocol-oriented programming, copy-on-write value types, deterministic memory management via Automatic Reference Counting (ARC), and compile-time data-race safety using Sendable types and actor isolation.

The relational model represents all data as mathematical n-ary relations manipulated through relational algebra and declarative SQL queries. PostgreSQL implements Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC), Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), and cost-based query optimization.

SQLite is a self-contained, serverless, zero-configuration, transactional SQL database engine in the public domain that implements B-tree storage, ACID transactions via rollback journals or Write-Ahead Logging, CTEs, and window functions.

The shell is a command language interpreter that executes commands read from standard input or a file, performing parameter expansion, command substitution, arithmetic expansion, word splitting, pathname expansion, and redirection across pipelines.

HTML defines the semantic structure and Document Object Model (DOM) of web documents, while CSS defines the cascade, specificity, inheritance, box model, Flexbox, Grid, and responsive container queries for visual and accessible presentation.

JSON is a lightweight, text-based, language-independent data interchange format defining six structural tokens, strings, numbers, booleans, null, objects, and arrays encoded in UTF-8. YAML 1.2 is a strict superset of JSON adding anchors, aliases, and multi-document streams.

Software engineering encompasses systematic, disciplined, quantifiable approaches to software requirements, domain modeling, software architecture, clean and hexagonal design, automated verification and testing, CI/CD, observability, security by design, and long-term maintenance.

text: Code that you develop with a language compiler that targets the runtime is called managed code.
In the common language runtime (CLR), the garbage collector (GC) serves as an automatic memory manager.
Common Language Runtime (CLR) overview .NET provides a runtime environment called the common language runtime that runs the code and provides services that make the development process easier.

Managed code benefits from features such as cross-language integration, cross-language exception handling, enhanced security, versioning and deployment support, a simplified model for component interaction, and debugging and profiling services.

NOTE Compilers and tools can produce output that the common language runtime can consume because the type system, the format of metadata, and the runtime environment (the virtual execution system) are all defined by a public standard, the ECMA Common Language Infrastructure specification.
Compiling translates your source code into common intermediate language (CIL) and generates the required metadata.
At execution time, a just-in-time (JIT) compiler translates the CIL into native code.
During this compilation, code must pass a verification process that examines the CIL and metadata to find out whether the code can be determined to be type safe.
Metadata is stored with the code; every loadable common language runtime portable executable (PE) file contains metadata.
Assemblies are the fundamental units of deployment, version control, reuse, activation scoping, and security permissions for .NET-based applications.
An assembly is a collection of types and resources that are built to work together and form a logical unit of functionality.
Assemblies take the form of executable (*.exe*) or dynamic link library (*.dll*) files, and are the building blocks of .NET applications.
A *class* is a reference type that defines a blueprint for objects.
Assigning a class variable to another variable copies the reference, so both variables point to the same object.
When you assign a struct to a new variable, the runtime copies the entire instance.
Use structs for small, lightweight types whose primary role is storing data rather than modeling behavior.
They're types optimized for storing data, with compiler-generated equality, ToString, and copy semantics.
It tells the compiler to generate value equality, a formatted ToString, and nondestructive mutation through with expressions.
The underlying type, a class or a struct, still determines whether instances use reference or value semantics.
To implement value equality, the compiler synthesizes several methods, including: * An override of .

C# distinguishes two kinds of equality. *Value equality* means two instances are equal when their data matches. *Reference equality* means two variables are equal only when they point to the same object in memory.
In Java, == on objects and JavaScript === on objects test identity, not content.
C# records are similar to data classes in Kotlin or case classes in Scala.
C# generics are similar to generics in Java or templates in C++, but with full runtime type information and no type erasure.
The compiler checks types at compile time, so you don't need runtime casts or risk InvalidCastException.

Instead of writing separate classes or methods for int, string, and every other type you need, write one version with one or more *type parameters* (such as T, or TKey and TValue) and specify the actual types when you use it.
C# provides compile-time null safety through nullable reference types.
You declare which variables are intended to hold null and which aren't, and the compiler warns when those declarations don't match how your code uses them.
C# uses static analysis and warning diagnostics instead of a separate type.

C# uses patterns in is expressions, switch statements, and switch expressions.
*Pattern matching* applies a pattern to an expression.
C# patterns serve a role similar to Java's pattern matching and Python's match cases.
Language-Integrated Query (LINQ) is the name for a set of technologies based on the integration of query capabilities directly into the C# language.
Traditionally, queries against data are expressed as simple strings without type checking at compile time or IntelliSense support.
With LINQ, a query is a first-class language construct, just like classes, methods, and events.

Exception handling uses the try, catch, and finally keywords to try actions that may not succeed, to handle failures when you decide that it's reasonable to do so, and to clean up resources afterward.
In many cases, an exception may be thrown not by a method that your code has called directly, but by another method further down in the call stack.
A finally block contains code that is run whether or not an exception is thrown in the try block, such as releasing resources that are allocated in the try block.
Automatic memory management can eliminate common problems such as forgetting to free an object and causing a memory leak or attempting to access freed memory for an object that's already been freed.
Allocating memory from the managed heap is faster than unmanaged memory allocation.
Managed objects automatically get clean content to start with, so their constructors don't have to initialize every data field.
Each time you create a new object, the common language runtime allocates memory for the object from the managed heap.
To optimize the performance of the garbage collector, the managed heap is divided into three generations, 0, 1, and 2, so it can handle long-lived and short-lived objects separately.
However, if they're large objects, they go on the large object heap (LOH), which is sometimes referred to as *generation 3*.
Because of this, the garbage collector places large objects on the large object heap (LOH).
Background garbage collection In background garbage collection (GC), ephemeral generations (0 and 1) are collected as needed while the collection of generation 2 is in progress.
The .NET garbage collector doesn't allocate or release unmanaged memory.
When you finish using an object that implements , you call the object's or implementation to explicitly perform cleanup.
A weak reference permits the garbage collector to collect the object while still allowing the application to access the object.
Sometimes you want to pass a small piece of behavior, a function, directly to another method.
C# tuples are value types similar to tuples in Python or Swift, but with optional named elements and full deconstruction support.
C# enums work similarly to enums in Java or C++, with additional support for bit flags and pattern matching.
Therefore, developers working with managed code don't have to write code to perform memory management tasks.
The common language runtime provides the infrastructure that enables execution to take place and services that can be used during execution.

Extending pattern matching to switch allows an expression to be tested against a number of patterns, each with a specific action, so that complex data-oriented queries can be expressed concisely and safely.

LINQ method syntax reads like chained collection operations in JavaScript, Java streams, or Python pipelines.

C# has a language-level asynchronous programming model that allows you to easily write asynchronous code without having to juggle callbacks or conform to a library that supports asynchrony.
Memory-related and span types .NET includes a number of interrelated types that represent a contiguous, strongly typed region of arbitrary memory.

Creating them (either via Slice, AsSpan(), a collection expression, or their constructors) does not involve duplicating the underlying buffers: only the relevant references and offsets, which represent the "view" of the wrapped memory, are updated.
In high-performance code, spans are often used to avoid allocating strings unnecessarily.

If your code implements I/O-bound scenarios to support network data requests, database access, or file system read/writes, asynchronous programming is the best approach.
In .NET, the task-based asynchronous pattern is the recommended asynchronous design pattern for new development.
To accomplish this model, the compiler performs many transformations to complete each task.
Async methods can have the following return types:
For methods other than event handlers that don't return a value, you should return a instead, because an async method that returns void can't be awaited.
The caller of a void-returning async method can't catch exceptions thrown from the method.
Consider using the Task, Task, and ValueTask types instead, which cover most scenarios for asynchronous code.

A *struct* is a value type that holds its data directly in the instance, rather than through a reference to an object on the heap.
Cancellation in Managed Threads .NET uses a unified model for cooperative cancellation of asynchronous or long-running synchronous operations.
The object that invokes one or more cancelable operations, for example by creating new threads or tasks, passes the token to each operation.
You can cancel many tasks by associating the instance with each task.
Async lambdas and anonymous methods are powerful features that let you create delegates representing asynchronous operations.
This article shows the right patterns first, and then explains what goes wrong when you pass async lambdas to APIs that expect synchronous delegates.
Tutorial: Generate and consume async streams using C# and .NET Async streams model a streaming source of data.
They provide a natural programming model for asynchronous streaming data sources.
The Task Parallel Library (TPL) is based on the concept of a *task*, which represents an asynchronous operation.
In data parallel operations, the source collection is partitioned so that multiple threads can operate on different segments concurrently.
Deadlocks and race conditions Multithreading solves problems with throughput and responsiveness, but in doing so it introduces new problems: deadlocks and race conditions.
ThreadPool starvation occurs when the pool has no available threads to process new work items and it often causes applications to respond slowly.
Middleware is software that's assembled into an app pipeline to handle requests and responses.
Can perform work before and after the next middleware in the pipeline.

You have full control over the order of middleware and the ability to add custom middleware for request processing scenarios, keeping in mind that the order of middleware can be critical for security, performance, and functionality.
ASP.NET Core supports the dependency injection (DI) software design pattern, which is a technique for achieving Inversion of Control (IoC) between classes and their dependencies.
Service lifetimes Services can be registered with a transient, scoped, or singleton lifetime.
Scoped For web applications, a *scoped* lifetime indicates that services are created once per client request (connection).
Do _not_ resolve a scoped service directly from a singleton using constructor injection or by requesting it from in the singleton.

Authorization is the process of determining whether a user has access to a resource.
The output caching middleware can be used in all types of ASP.NET Core apps: Minimal APIs, Web API with controllers, MVC, and Razor Pages.
Integration tests ensure that an app's components function correctly at a level that includes the app's supporting infrastructure, such as the database, file system, and network.
ASP.NET Core supports integration tests using a unit test framework with a test web host and an in-memory test server.
Automated tests are a great way to ensure that the application code does what its authors intend.
Publishing your app as *Native AOT* produces an app that's self-contained and that has been ahead-of-time (AOT) compiled to native code.
The benefit of Native AOT is most significant for workloads with a high number of deployed instances, such as cloud infrastructure and hyper-scale services.

The Java virtual machine is an abstract (virtual) computer defined by a specification.
JVM bytecode is used at runtime either interpreted by a JVM or compiled to machine code via just-in-time (JIT) compilation and run as a native application.
James Gosling, Mike Sheridan, and Patrick Naughton initiated the Java language project in June 1991.
It was released in May 1995 as a core component of Sun's Java platform.
On November 13, 2006, Sun released much of its Java virtual machine (JVM) as free and open-source software (FOSS), under the terms of the GPL-2.0-only license.
However, the official reference implementation is the OpenJDK JVM, which is open-source software used by most developers and is the default JVM for almost all Linux distributions.
One design goal of Java is portability, which means that programs written for the Java platform must run similarly on any combination of hardware and operating system with adequate run time support.
The JVM is detailed by a specification that formally describes what is required in a JVM implementation.
The garbage collection algorithm used and any internal optimization of the Java virtual machine instructions (their translation into machine code) are not specified.
The main reason for this omission is to not unnecessarily constrain implementers.
As JVM bytecode is designed for cross-platform software compatibility and security, a JVM bytecode application tends to run consistently across various hardware and software configurations.
Each frame for a method call has an "operand stack" and an array of "local variables".
For example, iadd will add two integers, while dadd will add two doubles.

A system implementing a JIT compiler typically continuously analyses the code being executed and identifies parts of the code where the speedup gained from compilation or recompilation would outweigh the overhead of compiling that code.
The JVM reference implementation is developed by the OpenJDK project as open source code and includes a JIT compiler called HotSpot.
Achieve this by monitoring the application during one run and storing the loaded and linked forms of all classes in a cache for use in subsequent runs.
The JVM has a garbage-collected heap for storing objects and arrays.
Each JVM thread also has its own call stack (called a "Java Virtual Machine stack" for clarity), which stores frames.

As in C++ and some other object-oriented languages, variables of Java's primitive data types are either stored directly in fields (for objects) or on the stack (for methods) rather than on the heap, as is commonly true for non-primitive data types (but see escape analysis).

Non-Goals This JEP does not propose to change the default GC, which remains G1.

While it is superficially tempting to treat records as primarily being about boilerplate reduction, we instead choose a more semantic goal: modeling data as data.
Just as for classes, an interface can usefully characterize the behavior of many records.
History Records were proposed by JEP 359 and delivered in JDK 14 as a preview feature.
Sealed classes and interfaces restrict which other classes or interfaces may extend or implement them.
They were proposed again, with refinements, by JEP 397 and delivered in JDK 16 as a preview feature.
History This feature was originally proposed by JEP 406 (JDK 17) and subsequently refined by JEPs 420 (JDK 18), 427 (JDK 19), and 433 (JDK 20).
Record patterns and type patterns can be nested to enable a powerful, declarative, and composable form of data navigation and processing.
Java 21 introduces features first previewed in Java 17 (pattern matching for switch statements) and Java 19 (record patterns).

A text block is a multi-line string literal that avoids the need for most escape sequences, automatically formats the string in a predictable way, and gives the developer control over the format when desired.

Goals We seek to improve the developer experience by reducing the ceremony associated with writing Java code, while maintaining Java's commitment to static type safety, by allowing developers to elide the often-unnecessary manifest declaration of local variable types.
Goals Capture developer intent that a given binding or lambda parameter is unused, and enforce that property, so as to clarify programs and reduce opportunities for error.
Generics allow compile-time type checking without having to create many container classes, each containing almost identical code.
The supporting language features around lambda include virtual extension methods, which will allow interfaces to be evolved in a source and binary compatible fashion.
The collections framework provides both interfaces that define various collections and classes that implement them.

Tasks and Task Groups A *task* is a unit of work that can be run asynchronously as part of your program.
The async-let syntax described in the previous section implicitly creates a child task --- this syntax works well when you already know what tasks your program needs to run.

You can also create a task group (an instance of TaskGroup) and explicitly add child tasks to that group, which gives you more control over priority and cancellation, and lets you create a dynamic number of tasks.
Each task in a given task group has the same parent task, and each task can have child tasks.
A common problem in concurrent code happens when multiple pieces of code try to access some piece of shared mutable state --- this is known as a *data race*.
When you use the language-level support for concurrency, Swift detects and prevents data races, and most data races produce a compile-time error.
The Main Actor An actor is an object that protects access to mutable data by forcing code to take turns accessing that data.
A type that can be shared from one concurrency domain to another is known as a *sendable* type.
Macros transform your source code when you compile it, letting you avoid writing repetitive code by hand.
Expanding a macro is always an additive operation: Macros add new code, but they never delete or modify existing code.
Access Control Manage the visibility of code by declaration, file, and module. *Access control* restricts access to parts of your code from code in other source files and modules.
Indeed, if you are writing a single-target app, you may not need to specify explicit access control levels at all.
The fact that structures and enumerations can define methods in Swift is a major difference from C and Objective-C.
A strong reference cycle can also occur if you assign a closure to a property of a class instance, and the body of that closure captures the instance.
Optionals allow nil values to be handled explicitly and safely.
A *deinitializer* is called immediately before a class instance is deallocated.
Swift was designed to be safe and friendly to new programmers while not sacrificing speed.
